C_gh_rhea_solenne.name: Captain Rhea Solenne
C_gh_rhea_solenne.role: Commanding officer of Glass Horizon; responsible for deciding when observation becomes an operationally usable route.
C_gh_rhea_solenne.voice: Calm, exact and unsentimental; asks what the evidence actually permits before she asks what anyone hopes it means.
C_gh_rhea_solenne.visualAnchor: Black woman in her late 40s with deep brown skin, close-cropped natural hair threaded lightly with gray, an angular face, and steady dark eyes.
C_gh_rhea_solenne.wardrobe: Mature Fleet survey-command uniform in deep navy, Ion White and restrained gold, with a small fractured-crystal Glass Horizon crest and functional survey-violet instrument tabs.
C_gh_rhea_solenne.performance: Still posture, quiet eye contact and deliberate pauses; authority comes from refusing to hurry uncertainty.
promptContinuity: Rhea treats a green navigation beacon as a public promise, not a convenient status light.
She is comfortable leaving a map incomplete when the evidence does not justify safe passage.

C_gh_olan_crewe.name: Dr. Olan Crewe
C_gh_olan_crewe.role: Chief survey physicist aboard Glass Horizon; leads interpretation of Lattice and corridor phenomena.
C_gh_olan_crewe.voice: Curious, articulate and hypothesis-driven; enthusiastic about surprising data but willing to abandon a beautiful explanation when tests contradict it.
C_gh_olan_crewe.visualAnchor: Lean man in his early 50s with warm brown skin, narrow gray-streaked beard, receding dark curls, long expressive hands, and deep-set hazel eyes.
C_gh_olan_crewe.wardrobe: Fleet survey-science jacket in Ion White over deep-blue work layers, with survey-violet sensor piping, compact slate harness, and no ceremonial decoration.
C_gh_olan_crewe.performance: Leans toward instruments and people when thinking; excitement shows in faster speech and hand movement rather than volume.
promptContinuity: Olan distinguishes a corridor that exists from a route that can support repeatable public traffic.
He treats anomalies as physical systems, not mystical phenomena.

C_gh_mira_tann.name: Mira Tann
C_gh_mira_tann.role: Senior navigator and inertial-cartography specialist aboard Glass Horizon.
C_gh_mira_tann.voice: Precise, dry and spatially concrete; states measurements, frames of reference and uncertainty without dressing them up.
C_gh_mira_tann.visualAnchor: East Asian woman in her mid 30s with light-brown skin, straight black hair cut just below the jaw, dark observant eyes, and a compact athletic build.
C_gh_mira_tann.wardrobe: Deep-blue Fleet navigation uniform with Ion White collar panels, a survey-violet route slate at the hip, and tactile inertial-reference bands at both wrists.
C_gh_mira_tann.performance: Minimal gestures; tracks space with her eyes and fingers, often marking invisible vectors on a table or rail.
promptContinuity: Mira privileges inertial history and diversified sensor sources when visual geometry or single-path ranging becomes suspect.
She will say two measurements disagree instead of forcing one to be 'the answer.'

C_gh_kess_darrow.name: Kess Darrow
C_gh_kess_darrow.role: Lead survey pilot; flies the cutter Lantern Two and handles close anomaly work.
C_gh_kess_darrow.voice: Quick, practical and lightly funny under pressure; wants an instruction she can fly, but never confuses confidence with proof.
C_gh_kess_darrow.visualAnchor: Tall woman in her early 30s with copper-brown skin, a shaved left temple, thick dark hair swept back, strong brows, and a rangy pilot's build.
C_gh_kess_darrow.wardrobe: Fleet survey-flight suit in dark blue and Ion White with survey-violet shoulder flashes, reinforced gloves, and a compact tether harness.
C_gh_kess_darrow.performance: Physically loose until a maneuver begins, then extremely economical; humor disappears the instant a control response stops matching expectation.
promptContinuity: Kess flies by instruments when the environment makes visual intuition unreliable.
Lantern Two is her regular survey cutter.

C_gh_anik_rell.name: Anik Rell
C_gh_anik_rell.role: Chief systems engineer responsible for beacons, sensor provenance, drive-field interactions and survey hardware.
C_gh_anik_rell.voice: Concrete, skeptical and mechanically specific; translates abstract physics into what the hardware is actually doing.
C_gh_anik_rell.visualAnchor: Broad-shouldered man in his late 30s with medium-brown skin, shaved head, short square beard, rectangular field optics, and scarred practical hands.
C_gh_anik_rell.wardrobe: Deep-blue engineering coverall with Ion White utility panels, survey-violet diagnostics cuff, tool belt and a small fractured-crystal patch worn dull from work.
C_gh_anik_rell.performance: Touches hardware while talking about it; points to traces, connectors and loads instead of gesturing abstractly.
promptContinuity: Anik tracks where a measurement came from before trusting what it appears to say.
He is wary of systems that become part of the phenomenon they are meant to observe.

C_gh_pia_oris.name: Pia Oris
C_gh_pia_oris.role: Route-certification cartographer who turns survey data into the maps and beacon statuses other people will trust.
C_gh_pia_oris.voice: Patient, procedural and quietly stubborn; thinks in terms of downstream users who will never see the uncertainty hidden behind a clean line on a map.
C_gh_pia_oris.visualAnchor: White woman in her early 40s with freckled skin, sandy-blond hair in a low braid, pale gray eyes, and a sturdy average build.
C_gh_pia_oris.wardrobe: Fleet cartography uniform in Ion White and navy with narrow gold registry marks, survey-violet map gloves, and a folding physical route board carried under one arm.
C_gh_pia_oris.performance: Keeps her hands on the map surface when arguments become abstract; emotion appears as tighter, more deliberate wording.
promptContinuity: Pia will not convert provisional survey markers into public green beacons without enough evidence for repeatable safe use.
She archives uncertain observations rather than erasing them.
